title: Looping and Totals
goal: In this lesson you will learn how to keep a running total inside a loop by adding to a variable each time through.
learn: Start a total at 0 before the loop
Add to the total inside the loop
Print the total after the loop finishes
idea: A running total (or accumulator) is a variable that grows as the loop runs. Start with total = 0 before the loop. Inside the loop, add the next number: total = total + n. After the loop, print total to see the sum. This pattern works for summing a range, adding scores from a list, or counting how many times something happened.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change range(1, 6) to range(1, 4). Press Run. The final total should be 6 (1+2+3).

quiz.question: Why set total = 0 before the loop?

options.text: Python requires every variable to be 0
So you have a clear starting sum to add onto

quiz.correct: Starting at 0 gives you a blank slate to accumulate into.
quiz.wrong: You need a starting value before you begin adding.

quiz.question: What does total = total + n do inside a loop?

options.text: It adds the current n into the running total

quiz.correct: Each pass adds the current value into total.
quiz.wrong: That line updates total by adding this trip’s number.

quiz.question: When should you usually print the final total?

options.text: Only inside an if with no loop

quiz.correct: After the loop, total has every value added in.
quiz.wrong: Print after the loop so you see the completed sum.

project.title: Piggy Bank
project.desc: Coins are [5, 10, 25, 10]. Loop to add them into total. Print each coin as you add it, then print the final total.
